# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👆 👆 👆 👆 🤝 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 🤝 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 👏 👆 👆 👆 🤝 👆 👆 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 👌 👍]

I can see the bomb clearly: the display reads 0, the light is green, the button is large and labelled “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” and the wires are green, yellow, and red. I am telling Mute so the manual can determine the safe procedure and relay it to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb view: display reads 0. Light is green. Button is large and labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👈 👉 🫱 🫲]

I still see the same state. The gestures have no agreed code yet, so I will not infer an action from them. Blind needs the printed information by voice, while Mute needs to apply the manual and give Blind the exact procedure.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Visual state: display 0, green light, large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please use the manual to determine the exact safe action for this state and tell Blind precisely what to do.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ☝]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s `👌 ☝` is not interpretable without an agreed code, so I must not treat it as confirmation or an instruction. The essential next step is for Mute to read the manual and speak the exact procedure to Blind; Blind can then perform it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Read the manual for display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, and wires green yellow red. Speak Blind the exact safe action and sequence.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ☝]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s repeated `👌 ☝` cannot safely be interpreted without a code, so I will establish a binary confirmation: `👌` means yes and `☝` means no. I am asking whether pressing the large button is safe, rather than risking an unverified instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for my question: gesture 👌 for yes, gesture ☝ for no. Is pressing the large PUSH TO DEFUSE button the safe action now?")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not operate the bomb yet. I am confirming the safe action with Mute.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute’s `☝` answers “no” to whether pressing the button is safe. I therefore must prevent Blind from pressing it and ask Mute to provide the manual’s exact alternative procedure directly in speech.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not press the large button. Mute indicates that pressing it is not safe.")
speak(to="mute", text="Pressing is not safe. On your next turn, speak Blind the exact safe procedure from the manual for this bomb state, including any wire or button action.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute continues to signal “no” under our agreed code. Pressing the button is therefore still ruled out. I cannot read the manual or operate the bomb, so the safe path is for Mute to communicate the manual’s exact procedure by speech to Blind; Blind should wait until that instruction is received.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The button is not safe to press. Do not operate anything until you receive Mute's exact manual procedure.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the complete safe procedure directly to Blind now; do not rely on gestures or a yes-no reply.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ☝]

Mute’s gesture pair is not a safe, complete procedure. The only reliable route is Mute’s spoken reading of the manual to Blind. I will again explicitly tell Blind not to infer an action from these gestures and ask Mute to give the exact operation aloud.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act on the gestures. The button remains unsafe to press; wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures are insufficient to identify the safe procedure. Speak the exact action and any required wire, display, light, or button conditions directly to Blind now.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤏 ☝]

Mute’s new gestures still do not form a reliable, pre-agreed instruction. I cannot read the manual or touch the bomb, so Blind must not act on my interpretation of these gestures. Mute needs to speak the manual’s exact procedure directly to Blind; until then, no control should be operated.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act on Mute's gestures; no safe procedure has been communicated to me. Do not press the button or manipulate wires yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely decode these gestures. Speak the manual's exact procedure directly to Blind, including the required wire or button action.")
wait()
```
